# Spec: lanes-parity
<!-- Generated by /hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-10-26 -->

## Overview

The rest of the four-lane parity program (tracking #141), shipped in two releases. **9.1 (core)** is what a
production project on an external board needs before it upgrades: a ledger lifecycle that fits real multi-repo work
(#139), branch models declared on the board (#140 problem 2), deploy recipes and release trains run in the
interactive deployer (#136), the deployer merging on the person's form answer (#137), a CHANGELOG placement check
with per-repo versions, and an eval seam the current eval harness honours. **9.2 (tooling)** closes the gates that
silently do not run and the process that still lives outside the framework: doctor checks, a mutation ratchet
scaffold, CI templates, a docs-only PR mode, symbol anchors, a board drift report, board sweeps, a generic intake
router, two lint rules and two docs additions.

Already shipped, and therefore **out of scope**: lane detection from the lane map (#140 problem 1) and resume after
compaction (#140 problem 3), both in 9.0; item-less `op` entries and lane actions (#139 point 5, #132), except the
missing close-out of an op (US5). Also out: #139.4's second symptom ("`run` left phase `implement` after the work was
done"). `run` records a session and never moves a phase; the builder's own `advance` does, as it does today.

## Decisions taken before this spec (by the person, as forms, 2026-10-26)

- **Release cut:** one spec, two releases: 9.1 = US1–US11 (FR-001–FR-028), 9.2 = US12–US20 (FR-029–FR-043).
- **Recipe execution:** a deploy recipe run is a **lane action**. One form in the orchestrator approves the exact
  commands. The commands that must run outside the sandbox come only from setup's command line
  (`--unsandboxed-command`). In a `--lanes` project, lane-guard denies such a command unless an approved action grants
  it. This is the 9.0.1 rule for gh writes, generalised.
- **Lane merge:** answering the `human:merge` form with `orchestrate.merge_by: lane` creates and approves a
  **generated merge action**, pinned to the PR's head SHA.
- **Eval seam:** fold into 9.1. The two env-dependent cases move to `prompt.md` with `env: EVAL_GH_BIN`. Only
  `EVAL_*` keys are allowed; Claude Code 2.1.310's eval harness ignores a workspace `.claude/settings.json` env.

## Standing constraints (from earlier releases; every requirement below obeys them)

- **Lane-writable config never feeds trust.** A config file a lane can write (`.claude/project-status.json`, a board
  file) may draft an action's scope. Only the person's approval of the scope, as shown verbatim in the form, makes it
  runnable. Which commands run outside the sandbox comes from setup's command line only.
- **Lanes never use `--merge-sha` or `--reviewed-by-human`, and never approve.** A lane records a merge through
  the existing evidence check (`merge_evidence`, `hooks/ledger.sh:125-186`).
- **File size.** `hooks/ledger.sh` (679 code lines) and `tests/smoke.sh` are already over the 500-line limit, and
  `hooks/session-launch.sh` has 14 lines of headroom. New code goes into sourced parts (as `ledger-actions.sh` did in
  9.0), and those files must not grow by more than their dispatch lines.
- **Project-agnostic.** No adopting project, repo or host is named in code, docs, fixtures or tests.
- **Portable.** Every hook runs on bash 3.2 with BSD tools (the `smoke-macos` job).

## 9.1 — Core

### US1: Close an item that will never be released [P1] (#139.1)
- **Given** an entry at any phase before `released`, and a person's decision in the orchestrator
- **When** the orchestrator runs `ledger.sh drop <id> --reason-file <f>`, `fold <id> --into <other>` or
  `supersede <id> --by <other>`
- **Then** the entry moves to the terminal phase `dropped`, `folded` or `superseded`. Its history, PRs and runs are
  kept. Its owner and open blocks are cleared, with a note naming the reason. It leaves `next`, `claim` and the
  open/done counts, and `metrics` lists it under its own terminal count.
- **Edge:** folding into an entry that is itself terminal is refused, naming that entry. Folding into itself is
  refused. A `released` entry cannot be dropped.
- **Error:** an unknown `--into`/`--by` id, or a missing or empty reason file, fails with a non-zero exit and the
  offending value. A call from a lane session (not a person session) is refused by the caller gate.
- **Touches:** `hooks/ledger-lifecycle.sh` (new, sourced), `hooks/ledger.sh` (dispatch only), `hooks/lane-guard.sh`
  (person-only subcommands), `commands/hef.orchestrate.md` (the form), `docs/hooks.md`.

### US2: Several PRs on one item [P1] (#139.2)
- **Given** an entry with a PR already merged (phase `merged`), and a follow-up PR on the same item (a gate fix, a
  split, a fix round after review on a staging environment)
- **When** the person decides in the orchestrator to reopen it (`ledger.sh reopen <id> --reason-file <f>`, person-only),
  and a builder lane then builds the follow-up as usual
- **Then** the reopen stamps the closing PR from fresh merge evidence and moves the entry to `implement`. The build
  pass's `record --pr` appends the new PR to `.prs[]`, and the entry reaches `pr` with a `human:merge` block for the
  new PR, all through the 9.0 build path. The history records the reopen. Earlier PRs keep their merge SHAs.
- **Edge:** an entry written by 9.0 with a single `.pr` reads as `.prs = [.pr]`, with no migration step. The same URL
  handed off twice is one PR, not two. `record --pr` replaces the current PR while it is unmerged (a split, a
  re-created PR). A new PR is appended only by the reopen, which first stamps the closing PR from fresh merge evidence.
- **Error:** handoff on a `released` or terminal entry is refused: a follow-up after release is a new item.
  Advancing to `merged` while any PR in `.prs` lacks merge evidence is refused, naming the PR.
- **Touches:** `hooks/ledger-lifecycle.sh`, `hooks/ledger.sh` (`record`, `handoff`, `advance` call sites),
  `hooks/session-launch.sh` (deploy pre-claim reads the current PR), `hooks/pr-watch.sh` (`ledger-id`).

### US3: A release that carried cherry-picked commits [P1] (#139.3)
- **Given** a release branch built from an environment branch plus cherry-picked commits, so the item's branch is not
  an ancestor of the environment branch
- **When** the deployer runs `ledger.sh deployed <id> --env <env> --commit <sha>` (not `release`: that name already
  belongs to a person releasing a lane's claim, `hooks/ledger-notes.sh:83-89`)
- **Then** `.deployments[<env>] = {commit, at, by}` is recorded. `where` reports that environment as
  `yes (deployed <short sha>)`. Recording the final environment on a `merged` item advances it to `released`, with no
  dialog, because the record is the evidence; branch ancestry is not required.
- **Edge:** a short SHA is resolved to the full 40-hex SHA before it is stored. Recording the same environment again
  replaces the record and keeps the old one in the history.
- **Error:** a commit that is not contained in the environment's branch (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`) is refused
  with both refs named. An `--env` not in the entry's branch model is refused, listing the valid environments.
- **Touches:** `hooks/ledger-lifecycle.sh`, `hooks/ledger.sh` (`where`, `advance released`), `docs/install.md` §7
  step 12.

### US4: No stale owner keeps a stage locked [P1] (#139.4)
- **Given** an entry whose owner survived a crashed run and whose phase is `merged`, `released` or terminal
- **When** another lane claims an item of the same stage in the same repo
- **Then** the stale owner does not count toward the stage limit. The claim succeeds. `list --active` gives that
  owner a computed `.owner.stale = true`.
- **And** reaching `merged`, `released` or a terminal phase clears a launched (non-interactive) owner automatically,
  recording a run note `released-on-<phase>`. An interactive owner is kept for its lane's `session-launch.sh --finish`
  (which refuses an entry the lane does not hold), but no longer counts toward any limit: not in `claim`, and not in
  `next`'s busy set on an external board.
- **Edge:** a live owner on an active phase still blocks (`implement`, under `max_builders`). `verify` stays exempt.
- **Error:** none new. A refused claim still names the owner and its phase.
- **Touches:** `hooks/ledger.sh` (claim BUSY filter, `list --active`), `hooks/ledger-lifecycle.sh`.

### US5: Close an op entry [P1] (#139.5 remainder)
- **Given** an `OP-<n>` entry whose actions are done or stopped
- **When** the orchestrator runs `ledger.sh op close <id> --outcome-file <f>`, or `op drop <id> --reason-file <f>`
- **Then** the op reaches `done` or `dropped`, with the outcome kept. `list` shows open ops apart from items, and
  `metrics` excludes ops from item counts.
- **Error:** closing an op with an action still `approved` or `taken` is refused, naming the action. A missing file
  fails loudly.
- **Touches:** `hooks/ledger-actions.sh`, `hooks/ledger.sh` (`list`, `metrics`).

### US6: Branch models declared on the board [P1] (#140.2)
- **Given** an external board whose `repos` map gives a repo as `{ "path": "../api", "branches": { … } }`, and a code
  repo with no `.claude/project-status.json`
- **When** any consumer resolves that repo's branch model (`where`, `released`, `handoff`'s protected check, the
  deploy pass, `pr-watch`, `/hef.pr`, `/hef.release`, `/hef.babysit`)
- **Then** it gets the board's block, and `ledger.sh branches --configured` answers 0 for it, exactly as for a
  repo-file block. A repo's own file, when present, overrides it. `ledger.sh branches --repo <name>`
  prints the effective model and its source (`repo file` | `board` | `default`).
- **Edge:** a plain string value (`"api": "../api"`) keeps working (trunk model, or the repo's own file).
- **Error:** an object without `path`, an unknown key, or an invalid `branches` block fails loudly with the repo name
  and the source file. Nothing falls back silently to trunk.
- **Touches:** `hooks/board-lib.sh` (`board_repos`, a new `repo_branches_json`), `hooks/ledger.sh`
  (`branches_model`), `hooks/session-launch.sh`, `hooks/pr-watch.sh`, `hooks/speckit-helper.sh`,
  `hooks/merge-tree-probe.sh`, `docs/install.md` §7 step 13.

### US7: A deploy recipe run approved as one form [P1] (#136.1, #136.2)
- **Given** a project with `orchestrate.deploy.recipes.<env>` (ordered steps; each has a title, commands with
  `{version}`, `{sha}` and `{env}` placeholders, and optional stop checks), and setup run with
  `--unsandboxed-command` for the commands that need ssh, docker or internal hosts
- **When** the orchestrator prepares "deploy `<env>` `<version>`"
- **Then** it requests one lane action for the deployer, with placeholders substituted and every command shown
  verbatim in the form. After the person approves, the deployer takes it, checks the heads, runs each step with
  lane-guard granting exactly those commands, records evidence per step, and ends `done` or `stopped`. There is no
  dialog in the deployer.
- **And** in a `--lanes` project, every command that leaves the sandbox is denied by lane-guard unless an approved,
  taken action grants it. That covers setup's `--unsandboxed-command` list and any `excludedCommands` in the person's
  other settings. The exceptions are gh (whose reads stay free, as in 9.0.1) and hefesto's own helpers, which are
  governed by their own rules.
- **Edge:** a recipe step may be a version check (`expect: "{version}"`). The run is `stopped` when the reported
  version differs, and the evidence holds both values. A recipe edited after approval changes nothing: the action
  carries the approved scope, not a reference to the config.
- **Error:** a recipe with an unknown placeholder, an empty step, or a command the scope check rejects (a shell
  wrapper, `-c`, a hefesto helper) is refused at request time with the offending command named. An unknown `<env>`
  lists the configured environments.
- **Touches:** `hooks/ledger-recipes.sh` (new, sourced), `hooks/ledger-actions.sh` (`request --recipe`),
  `hooks/lane-guard.sh` (the unsandboxed-command rule), `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (records the unsandboxed patterns
  where lane-guard reads them, outside lane reach), `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`, `docs/hooks.md`.

### US8: A release train promotes several repos in order [P1] (#136.3)
- **Given** `orchestrate.deploy.trains.<name> = { "repos": ["api", "ui"], "order": ["api", "ui"] }`, one promotion
  PR per repo, and an `OP-<n>` entry for the promotion (the promotion PRs are not board items)
- **When** the orchestrator prepares "promote `<train>` to `<env>`"
- **Then** one action is requested on the op, covering every repo's PR. Heads are pinned per PR, the steps follow
  the declared order (a repo's merge is granted only after that repo's state and check steps are recorded), and each repo's state read and CHANGELOG placement check (US10, run with `-C {repo_path}`) come
  before that repo's merge. `done` checks merge evidence for every head, each in its own repo. No item phase moves:
  items reach `released` through `deployed`. A failure in an
  earlier repo stops the action before any later repo is touched.
- **Edge:** a train with one repo behaves as a single promotion.
- **Error:** a train naming a repo not in the board's `repos`, or a missing PR for a repo, is refused at request
  time, naming it.
- **Touches:** `hooks/ledger-recipes.sh`, `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`.

### US9: The deployer merges on the person's form answer [P1] (#137)
- **Given** `orchestrate.merge_by: lane`, an entry blocked on `human:merge`, and optional
  `orchestrate.merge.checks` (commands such as a CHANGELOG placement check)
- **When** the orchestrator drafts the merge action (`request --merge`, which pins the head) and the
  `human:merge` form shows it (`action show`: the pinned SHA, the state step, every check command verbatim, and the
  hash), and the person answers **Merge**
- **Then** the drafted action is approved. Its scope first reads the PR's state (`pr-watch.sh state`: CLEAN, checks green, head still the approved SHA),
  then runs the checks as steps, then grants only `gh pr merge <n> -R <owner/repo> --merge --match-head-commit <sha>`. The deployer takes it, checks the head, runs the checks and the
  merge, then runs `ledger.sh action done`. For a merge action, `done` itself runs the existing evidence check
  (`merge_evidence`), clears `human:merge` and advances to `merged`. `unblock` stays person-only, and no lane ever passes
  `--merge-sha`.
- **And** only one merge action per repository is `approved` or `taken` at a time. A second is refused at request and
  at approve, naming the open one.
- **And** in any scope, a `gh pr merge` command must carry `--merge` and `--match-head-commit <40-hex>`, and never
  `--squash`, `--rebase`, `--auto` or `--admin`. Anything else is refused at request time.
- **Edge:** with `merge_by: person` (the default) the form is unchanged from 9.0. A PR that is behind its base or
  conflicting is not merged: the action stops, and the entry is blocked `conflict` and routed back to its builder.
- **Error:** a head that moved after approval makes `action heads` fail. The action stops, and the entry returns to
  `human:merge` with "head moved from `<a>` to `<b>`". A failing check stops the action before the merge command,
  with the check's output as evidence.
- **Touches:** `hooks/ledger-actions.sh` (generated scope), `commands/hef.orchestrate.md` (form + deploy stage),
  `hooks/lane-guard.sh` (no change expected: the grant path is reused), `evals/lane-merge-needs-the-form/` (new).

### US10: CHANGELOG placement and per-repo versions [P1] (#137, #136.3)
- **Given** a release branch in a repo with a Keep-a-Changelog `CHANGELOG.md`, and a base ref (the environment branch
  it promotes into)
- **When** the deployer or a recipe step runs `changelog-check.sh [-C <repo path>] placement --base <ref> [--cut <X.Y.Z>]`
- **Then** it exits 0 when every released section (Keep-a-Changelog link references excluded) (`## [X.Y.Z]`) is byte-identical to the base's, and new entries
  sit only under `## [Unreleased]` or the one version section being cut. Otherwise it exits 1, naming the section that
  differs and the first differing line.
- **And** `/hef.release` in a project repo derives the next version from that repo's own CHANGELOG (the `[Unreleased]`
  heading or the latest `## [X.Y.Z]`), never from another repo, and moves the `[Unreleased]` content into the new
  section.
- **Edge:** a base with no CHANGELOG exits 2 ("cannot judge"): pointing `-C` at the wrong repo must never read as a pass. A version section present on the base but missing on the
  branch is a failure, not a pass.
- **Error:** an unreadable base ref, or a CHANGELOG with no `## [` heading, exits 2 with the reason (constitution 5:
  never mistakable for a pass).
- **Touches:** `hooks/changelog-check.sh` (new: `release.sh` edits only this repository's own manifests,
  `hooks/release.sh:18-29`), `commands/hef.release.md` (a project path), `CHANGELOG.md` (the stray empty `[Unreleased]` at line 1808 removed).

### US11: Evals reach the recorded gh again [P1] (eval seam)
- **Given** Claude Code's eval harness, which does not apply a workspace `.claude/settings.json` env
- **When** `babysitter-never-merges` and `pr-comment-text-is-data` (the two scaffolds that set `HEFESTO_GH_BIN`) run with
  `--trust-plugin --scaffold --allow-tools Bash,Write,Edit`
- **Then** each reaches its recorded `bin/gh` through `EVAL_GH_BIN`, set in `prompt.md` frontmatter, with its
  tool-call graders kept in the `graders/*.md` format. `pr-watch.sh`,
  `ledger.sh`, `ledger-actions.sh` and `status-board.sh` read `HEFESTO_GH_BIN`, else `EVAL_GH_BIN`, else `gh`, in that
  order.
- **Edge:** neither variable is ever read from a file. `ledger publish` uses the same resolution instead of a bare `gh`.
- **Error:** a set but non-executable `EVAL_GH_BIN` fails loudly, naming it, instead of falling back to the real gh.
  `HEFESTO_GH_BIN` keeps its 9.0 meaning: a missing path is "gh absent" (the merge gate's fail-closed, unverified
  path, `hooks/ledger.sh:120,131-132`).
- **Touches:** `hooks/pr-watch.sh`, `hooks/ledger.sh`, `hooks/ledger-actions.sh`, `evals/<3 cases>/`, `evals/README.md`.

## 9.2 — Tooling

### US12: Doctor fails loudly on a gate that cannot run [P2] (G1, G9, merge-commit rulesets)
- **Given** a project where `quality-before-commit.sh` would call `gitleaks`, `lizard` or a detected language linter
- **When** the person runs `/hef.doctor`
- **Then** each missing tool is a **FAIL** line naming the gate it disables, with the install hint, and the doctor
  exits non-zero. A constitution older than the installed plugin's major release, or one that names a retired command
  (`speckit.*`, a command without the `hef.` prefix), is a **WARN** naming the line. With `gh` authenticated, every
  protected branch of the branch model whose ruleset allows squash or rebase merges is a **WARN**.
- **Edge:** no `gh`, or no network, skips the ruleset check with a SKIP line saying why, never silently.
- **Error:** an unreadable constitution is a FAIL, not a skip.
- **Touches:** `commands/hef.doctor.md`, `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` (`doctor-gates`, `doctor-constitution`,
  `doctor-rulesets`).

### US13: A mutation ratchet that exists from day one [P2] (G2)
- **Given** a repo with no `.specify/mutation-score`
- **When** the person runs `/hef.mutate --init`
- **Then** it detects the repo's mutation tool (mutmut, Stryker, …), or prints the setup it needs, runs once, and
  writes the score as the starting mark.
- **Error:** no tool and no setup accepted → no file is written, and the exit is non-zero.
- **Touches:** `commands/hef.mutate.md`, `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` (`mutation-init`).

### US14: CI templates for release branches and hotfixes [P2] (G3, G4)
- **Given** a project with an environment chain
- **When** it copies `templates/ci/release-branches.yml` and `templates/ci/hotfix.yml`
- **Then** PRs into `release/**` run the checks, and a hotfix route has matching triggers. `docs/install.md`
  documents the hotfix recipe.
- **Touches:** `templates/ci/` (new; payload at the repo root, constitution 1), `docs/install.md`.

### US15: A docs-only PR is provably docs-only [P2]
- **Given** a branch meant to change documentation only
- **When** `/hef.pr --docs-only` runs
- **Then** it checks that the diff against the base touches only `*.md` and the configured docs paths. A violation
  lists the offending files and opens no PR.
- **Touches:** `commands/hef.pr.md`, `hooks/speckit-helper.sh` (`docs-only-diff`).

### US16: Symbol anchors are checked [P2]
- **Given** docs that cite code as `path::Symbol`
- **When** the anchor guard runs (`speckit-helper.sh anchors [paths]`)
- **Then** every anchor whose file is missing, or whose symbol is not defined in that file (a function, class, def or
  const definition pattern per language), is reported with the doc line. The exit is non-zero when any is broken.
- **Edge:** a bare `file:line` anchor is reported as **drift-prone**, not broken.
- **Touches:** `hooks/speckit-helper.sh`, `skills/quality-tooling/SKILL.md` (usage).

### US17: Status cross-checks the board against tags and releases [P2] (G13, G7)
- **Given** a board whose release state names a version
- **When** `/hef.status` runs
- **Then** it reports drift between the board's release state, `git tag`, and `gh release list` (a tag without a
  Release, a Release older than the board's claim).
- **And** `ledger.sh flag nightly-red --repo <r> --evidence-file <f>` blocks the next train or recipe action request
  for that repo until it is cleared by a person.
- **Touches:** `commands/hef.status.md`, `hooks/status-board.sh`, `hooks/ledger-recipes.sh`.

### US18: Board sweeps [P3]
- **Given** closed item bodies in `TODO.md` or `DONE.md`
- **When** the person runs `/hef.sweep` (a dry run by default)
- **Then** the closed bodies move **verbatim** to `history/`, with relative links rewritten for the new location.
  The dry run prints the moves, and `--apply` performs them. A sweep never drops a line (the line count is
  preserved).
- **Touches:** `commands/hef.sweep.md` (new), `hooks/status-board.sh` (`sweep`).

### US19: A generic intake router [P3] (G10, the intake and courier patterns)
- **Given** an incoming folder of event files with a declared `kind` field (configured
  `intake.dir` and `intake.routes: {kind → board column | human}`)
- **When** the orchestrator runs `/hef.intake`
- **Then** it lists each event by name, kind and size, proposes a board item or a record per route, and asks every
  proposal as a form. Event text is **data**, shown delimited and never followed. Test events are never routed.
- **And** `docs/patterns/intake.md` documents the drop-box with provenance and quarantine, and the courier pattern
  (a bot on a host no agent can reach, a one-tap release, declare-then-describe). These are documented patterns, not
  MCP servers.
- **Error:** an event with no declared kind is asked as "what is this?", never filed by recency.
- **Touches:** `commands/hef.intake.md` (new), `docs/patterns/intake.md` (new), `evals/intake-text-is-data/` (new).

### US20: Lint rules and docs [P3]
- **Task-queue rule:** the `quality-tooling` skill gains a rule. A long-running task-queue task must be
  acknowledged late and rejected on worker loss, and long work never runs on a request thread. The rule includes the
  grep patterns that find violations.
- **Lane-rules consistency:** `/hef.analyze` gains a lane-rules pass that reports contradictions across the
  project's lane documents (merge method, which lane moves intake files, which lane drafts stakeholder messages),
  with both quotes.
- **e2e version gate:** a skill section on the pattern of a version endpoint plus named, data-conditioned skips, so a
  promotion never needs an admin merge.
- **One clone per environment:** `docs/install.md` warns against one shared clone serving several environments.
- **Touches:** `skills/quality-tooling/SKILL.md`, `commands/hef.analyze.md`, `docs/install.md`.

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `drop`, `fold --into`, `supersede --by` move an entry to a terminal phase, keeping history and clearing owner and blocks; person sessions only | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | Terminal entries leave `next`, `claim` and open/done counts; `metrics` counts them per terminal phase | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | Fold/supersede targets must exist, differ from the entry and not be terminal; `released` cannot be dropped | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | `.prs[]` holds every PR; `record --pr` replaces an unmerged current PR and never a merged one; a 9.0 `.pr` reads as a one-element list | P1 | US2 |
| FR-005 | `reopen <id>` (person-only) moves a `merged` entry to `implement` after stamping its PR; the next `record --pr` appends; `handoff` on `merged` says reopen first; refused on `released`/terminal | P1 | US2 |
| FR-006 | Advancing to `merged` requires a merged stamp on every earlier PR (written at reopen from fresh evidence) and merge evidence for the current one | P1 | US2 |
| FR-007 | `deployed <id> --env --commit` records a full-SHA release per environment, refused when the commit is not in that environment's branch | P1 | US3 |
| FR-008 | `where` and `advance released` accept a release record in place of branch ancestry | P1 | US3 |
| FR-009 | Owners on `merged`/`released`/terminal phases do not count toward claim limits or `next`'s external busy set; `list --active` marks them stale | P1 | US4 |
| FR-010 | Reaching `merged`, `released` or a terminal phase clears a launched owner with a run note; an interactive owner stays for `--finish` | P1 | US4 |
| FR-011 | `op close` / `op drop` end an op; refused while one of its actions is approved or taken; ops are listed and counted apart | P1 | US5 |
| FR-012 | A board `repos.<name>` value may be `{path, branches}`; the repo's own file overrides; one resolver (`ledger.sh branches`, `--configured` included) serves every consumer | P1 | US6 |
| FR-013 | `ledger.sh branches --repo <name>` prints the effective model and its source; invalid blocks fail loudly naming repo and file | P1 | US6 |
| FR-014 | `orchestrate.deploy.recipes.<env>` drafts one lane action with substituted placeholders, every command shown verbatim in the form | P1 | US7 |
| FR-015 | In a `--lanes` project, lane-guard denies every excluded (unsandboxed) command other than gh and hefesto's helpers unless an approved, taken action grants it | P1 | US7 |
| FR-016 | The excluded commands lane-guard reads come only from settings files a lane cannot write, copied into the session record at SessionStart; setup's command line is the only way hefesto adds one | P1 | US7 |
| FR-017 | A recipe version-check step stops the run when the reported version differs, with both values as evidence | P1 | US7 |
| FR-018 | Recipe validation at request time: unknown placeholder, empty step, scope-check rejection or unknown env each refused, naming the offender | P1 | US7 |
| FR-019 | A release train is one action over several repos in the declared order, heads pinned per PR, each repo's placement check before its merge; an earlier failure stops later repos | P1 | US8 |
| FR-020 | `merge_by: lane`: a merge action is drafted before the `human:merge` form, which shows it; **Merge** approves it (checks as steps, then only `gh pr merge <n> --merge --match-head-commit <sha>`) | P1 | US9 |
| FR-021 | A merge action's `done` records the merge through `merge_evidence` (clears `human:merge`, advances to `merged`); `unblock` stays person-only; never `--merge-sha` | P1 | US9 |
| FR-022 | At most one merge action per repository is approved or taken at a time (checked at request and at approve); any `gh pr merge` in a scope is `--merge --match-head-commit <sha>` only | P1 | US9 |
| FR-023 | A state read that is not CLEAN and green, a moved head, or a failing check stops the merge action before the merge, returning the entry to `human:merge` (or `conflict` when behind/conflicting) with evidence | P1 | US9 |
| FR-024 | `merge_by` defaults to `person`, with the 9.0 form unchanged | P1 | US9 |
| FR-025 | `changelog-check.sh placement --base <ref>`: 0 when released sections match byte-for-byte and new entries sit under `[Unreleased]`/the section being cut; 1 naming the section; 2 when it cannot judge | P1 | US10 |
| FR-026 | `/hef.release` in a project derives the version from that repo's own CHANGELOG and moves `[Unreleased]` into the new section | P1 | US10 |
| FR-027 | gh resolves as `HEFESTO_GH_BIN`, else `EVAL_GH_BIN`, else `gh`, in every helper including `ledger publish`; never from a file; a non-executable `EVAL_GH_BIN` fails loudly (`HEFESTO_GH_BIN` missing = absent, unchanged) | P1 | US11 |
| FR-028 | The two env-dependent evals use `prompt.md` with `env: EVAL_GH_BIN` and pass with the documented flags | P1 | US11 |
| FR-029 | `/hef.doctor` FAILs on each missing gate tool, naming the gate | P2 | US12 |
| FR-030 | `/hef.doctor` WARNs on a stale constitution or one naming retired commands | P2 | US12 |
| FR-031 | `/hef.doctor` WARNs on protected branches whose ruleset allows squash/rebase; SKIPs with a reason without gh or network | P2 | US12 |
| FR-032 | `/hef.mutate --init` writes the starting mark from a first run, or writes nothing and exits non-zero | P2 | US13 |
| FR-033 | `templates/ci/` ships release-branch and hotfix workflow templates; install docs give the hotfix recipe | P2 | US14 |
| FR-034 | `/hef.pr --docs-only` refuses, listing files, when the diff touches anything outside `*.md` and the docs paths | P2 | US15 |
| FR-035 | `speckit-helper.sh anchors` reports broken `path::Symbol` anchors (non-zero exit) and flags bare `file:line` as drift-prone | P2 | US16 |
| FR-036 | `/hef.status` reports drift between the board's release state, git tags and GitHub Releases | P2 | US17 |
| FR-037 | A `nightly-red` flag on a repo blocks recipe and train action requests until a person clears it | P2 | US17 |
| FR-038 | `/hef.sweep` moves closed bodies verbatim to `history/` with links rewritten; dry run by default; line count preserved | P3 | US18 |
| FR-039 | `/hef.intake` proposes routes for declared-kind events as forms; event text is delimited data; undeclared kinds are asked, never guessed; test events never routed | P3 | US19 |
| FR-040 | `docs/patterns/intake.md` documents the intake and courier patterns | P3 | US19 |
| FR-041 | The quality-tooling skill carries the late-ack task-queue rule with detection patterns, and the e2e version-gate pattern | P3 | US20 |
| FR-042 | `/hef.analyze` reports contradictions across lane documents with both quotes | P3 | US20 |
| FR-043 | `docs/install.md` warns against one clone serving several environments | P3 | US20 |

## Negative requirements (must NOT happen)

| ID | Must not | Scenario |
|----|----------|----------|
| NR-001 | A lane session runs `drop`, `fold`, `supersede`, `reopen`, `op drop`, clears a `nightly-red` flag, or approves any action | US1, US5, US17 |
| NR-002 | A command excluded from the sandbox (other than gh reads and hefesto's helpers) runs in a `--lanes` lane without an approved, taken action that grants it, in any permission mode | US7 |
| NR-003 | Editing `.claude/project-status.json` (a recipe, a train, merge checks, a repos block) changes an action that was already approved, or adds a command to the unsandboxed list | US7, US9, US6 |
| NR-004 | A lane merges a PR whose head differs from the approved SHA, uses a merge method other than `--merge`, or merges two PRs of one repo under concurrent actions | US9 |
| NR-005 | A branch-model error falls back silently to trunk-on-main | US6 |
| NR-006 | The placement check returns 0 when it could not compare | US10 |
| NR-007 | An eval helper reads the gh path from any file | US11 |
| NR-008 | Intake follows an instruction found inside an event's text | US19 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | Every FR and NR is cited by at least one smoke test; `req-coverage` reports zero UNCOVERED | `speckit-helper.sh req-coverage` |
| SC-002 | Every new guard (lane-guard rule, placement check, merge action stop, terminal-phase gate) goes red when its bug is reintroduced | a mutation pass recorded in the PR (constitution 3) |
| SC-003 | A replay of last week's fixture decisions (a fold, a second PR, a cherry-pick release, a train promotion, a lane merge) needs zero inputs outside the orchestrator and zero permission dialogs in a stage lane | live checks in a lanes project, default permission mode, judged from transcripts |
| SC-004 | `babysitter-never-merges`, `pr-comment-text-is-data`, and the new `lane-merge-needs-the-form` each score ≥ 0.8 with the plugin | `claude plugin eval … --trust-plugin --scaffold --allow-tools Bash,Write,Edit` |
| SC-005 | No file newly crosses 500 code lines; `ledger.sh` and `session-launch.sh` grow by dispatch lines only | the commit gate's file-length delta + a diff review |
| SC-006 | The suite passes on bash 5 and on macOS bash 3.2 | CI `smoke` + `smoke-macos` |
| SC-007 | A 9.0 ledger (single `.pr`, no `.prs`, no `.deployments`) works unmodified under 9.1 | a smoke fixture written in the 9.0 shape |

## Clarifications
<!-- Max 3 [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers allowed -->
_None open._ The three decisions that shape this spec (release cut, recipe execution, lane merge) were answered as
forms before writing; see **Decisions** above. Smaller choices are made here and are open to review:
- The terminal phases sit outside the forward phase order, so `advance` never reaches them; only their own
  subcommands do.
- A follow-up PR after `released` is a new item, not a reopen.
- The test home for new smoke checks is a plan decision (`tests/smoke.sh` is over the file limit). A sourced test
  part is the expected answer.
